version.reason: `block.difficulty` is not gated by language version; the interesting axis is the EVM target, since the Paris rename is what solc warns about.

expected_solc_divergence.reason: solc 0.8.36 declines the Frontier target outright ('Invalid EVM version requested'), which is an error, while slang compiles the input. Unrelated to `block.difficulty`: solc never looks at the source on this target.

solc warns that 'Support for EVM versions older than constantinople is deprecated', which slang has no equivalent for, so slang reports nothing at all on these targets. Unrelated to `block.difficulty`.

This is the case the test is about: from Paris, solc warns that 'difficulty' was replaced by 'prevrandao'. Slang keeps `block.difficulty` available on every target without a diagnostic, so it stays silent where solc warns.
